b: p
Late night, I get in a Didi (Chinese Uber) and kind of mumble “man, I’m so tired.”
p
The driver, maybe 50-something, been driving since probably 7am, looks at me in the mirror and says:
p
“You young people always tired. Tired from what?”
p
I laughed it off. Then on the walk home I actually tried to answer him, and I couldn’t.
p

I hadn’t done much that week. What I had done was think. About my future, whether I’m on the right path, whether I should start something, go to the gym, switch plans… all day, every day. Then I’d go to bed feeling like I’d worked a construction shift.
p
He worked 12+ hours physically and was fine. I sat down all day and was exhausted.
p
I think a lot of us aren’t tired from doing too much. We’re tired from thinking too much and doing too little.
p
Three things that actually helped me:
p

-close your tabs:Write down every decision you’ve been avoiding and make the small ones today, even imperfectly. A bad decision you made weighs less than a good one you’re still carrying
-Do something physical daily: Walk, gym, cook, clean. Your brain needs time off too
-Finish before you start: Before starting a new plan or routine, finish one small thing you already started.
p
Funny part: when I felt like this, I used to watch more self-improvement content. Which just gave me more stuff to think about.
p
Anyone else get called out by a random stranger like this?
